newsitem.title: HONG KONG: The end is nigh - as Brits lose to China at rugby.
newsitem.headline: The end is nigh - as Brits lose to China at rugby.

text.p: The end of empire could not have been felt more painfully. The stiff upper lip quivered.
As the handover to China of Hong Kong, the last jewel of the former British empire, looms on July 1, China hit the colonialists where it really hurts -- on the rugby field.
China's People's Liberation Army troops gave the British garrison men their comeuppance in an international Tens rugby match in the colony's most important rugby week of the year.
Tuesday's skirmish between the outgoing and incoming military forces in Hong Kong ended with a 12-7 victory for the Chinese.
In the Battle of Hong Kong, the Black Watch, Scotland's senior highland regiment, came off second best.

Despite scenes which saw hefty Scottish forwards lumbering for the try line, and swatting away tackles from their elfish opponents, speed and agility told in the end. Scorer of the winning injury-time try, Shi Shuai, was euphoric. "I just thought about making the line -- I had to score that try," he said.
"I've only been playing rugby for two years and this is my first try in an international game."
This is hardly surprising -- the average age of the players in the team is 22, and the PLA Sports Institute team was only founded at the end of 1993.
To date, its international clashes have included playing visiting teams from Taiwan, Hong Kong, and Australia -- the Australian Aboriginal Schoolboys, not the Wallabies.

The match was watched by Major General Bryan Dutton, and Black Watch commanding officer Lieutenant Colonel Alasdair Loudon, who was gracious in defeat but noted that the PLA had a massive pool of young men to draw from.
"They have two million people to pick from and we have just 500 here, but I think we were just as fit as them," he said.
"It was a terrific game and we wanted to win. The players were going for it and did not hold back on the tackles."

"We couldn't have wanted a better first fixture. I think it makes a very nice point that in the first game we play in the Hong Kong Tens we're playing the PLA, who take over from us on July 1," Loudon said.
On that day, after more than 150 years of British rule, the defence of Hong Kong will be in the hands of the PLA.
The Hong Kong Tens are a prelude to the Rugby World Cup Sevens, which start in Hong Kong on Friday and form one of the biggest sporting and social events on the Hong Kong calendar.
The PLA Sports Institute team from Guangzhou in China's neighbouring Guangdong Province ran in a try in injury time to scupper a diplomatic 7-7 draw.

The Black Watch, playing under the banner of the Royal Highlanders, had walked onto the field behind two pipers playing Scotland the Brave and their spirited style of play had the PLA on the defensive in the early stages.

A try by Tony Woods, converted by Billy Paterson, gave them the lead at the start of the second half, but the nimbler Chinese came back with a converted try by Liu Yong before Shi went in at the corner for the victory.
